name: AH-1Z Viper
summary: The Marine Corps' twin-engine attack helicopter, the final evolution of the Cobra line, sharing engines, tail boom and rotor system with the UH-1Y.

wings: Long stub wings with weapon stations and AIM-9 rails at the tips
engines: Two engines blended along the top of the narrow fuselage
Exhausts angled up and outward behind the engine fairings
fuselage: Very narrow fuselage with tandem stepped cockpits
Target sight turret ball on the nose and a three-barrel 20 mm turret under the chin
tail: Four-blade tail rotor on a tall fin
Small horizontal stabilizers on the tail boom

tellTales: Narrow tandem-seat gunship on skids with a four-blade main rotor
Long stub wings with missile rails at the tips
Sensor ball on the very tip of the nose above a chin gun turret

confusedWith.howToTell: The Viper is slimmer and sits on skids; the Apache has wheels and a tailwheel, bulky side engine pods and a box-shaped nose turret.
Both share engines, rotor and tail, but the Viper has a narrow tandem gunship body with stub wings while the Venom has a wide side-by-side cockpit and troop cabin.
The single-engine Cobra has two blades and one engine; the AH-1Z has four blades and twin engines.

usCount.source: USMC H-1 program: 349 AH-1Z/UH-1Y delivered, ~189 AH-1Z (NAVAIR / FlightGlobal 2026)
